clue.text: Leave session of golf confused

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the words of golf are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer walks off the course in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a computer session and depart from it is the phrasal verb used for signing out of a system.

clue.text: Found at the end of a flight

definitions.text: Found at the end of a flight

parts.words: Found at the end of a flight
parts.note: the top of a flight of stairs has a platform, and an aeroplane flight ends by touching down

explanation.surface: Something discovered after a trip by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a stairway's platform and an aircraft's touchdown come at the close of a flight.

clue.text: Prepared vegan rice and beef

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked over, so the letters of vegan rice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A menu offering vegan rice alongside meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat beside vegan rice, but it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a complaint, a cause for protest.

clue.text: What a cricketer does when not in WC

definitions.text: What a cricketer does when not in WC

parts.words: What a cricketer does when not in WC
parts.note: a cricket team not in to bat is out on the field, and WC hints at Winston Churchill's speech

explanation.surface: A cricketer's activity when not in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side that is not 'in' (batting) stops the ball; WC is Winston Churchill, whose 1940 speech gives this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers who are not batting spend their time catching and stopping the ball in the outfield.

clue.text: City in Switzerland revolutionary for taking small denominations

parts.note: Chur is the capital of the Swiss canton of Graubünden
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A Swiss town's radical takes on small coins or banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denominations' looks like money but means religious bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious denominations such as Methodist or Baptist are each a separate Christian body or sect.

clue.text: Musical shock

definitions.meaning: the 1960s rock musical of that name
a thick mass, as in a shock of ...

explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s hippie show is a famous musical, and a shock is a thick head of locks.

clue.text: Started once more to kick into the long grass

indicators.note: into puts the kick inside the grass word

parts.note: reed is a tall grass
to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: Restarting a plan just to postpone it indefinitely.
explanation.walkthrough: Kicking into the long grass is the British idiom for shelving an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebooting a computer means starting it up again, and the word is now used of anything restarted.

clue.text: Range of first-hand complaints

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of hand

parts.note: ills are ailments or complaints

explanation.surface: A whole set of grumbles heard directly.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain range is a line of high ground, a chain of peaks and slopes.

clue.text: Lay brown-coated copper line

indicators.note: coated means covered on the outside, so the brown word goes round the copper and line letters

parts.note: to sear is to brown meat quickly
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Describing a copper cable with a brown sheath laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb but is the adjective, as in lay preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay means non-clerical, not belonging to the clergy, as worldly matters are opposed to religious ones.

clue.text: Sounds like I'm surrounded by features

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits within it, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: facial features include noses
I'm reads as 'I am', so the letter I is the thing surrounded

explanation.surface: Someone says they feel hemmed in by attractions or characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises and sounds are close synonyms for things heard.

clue.text: Infernal boil treated with acid

indicators.note: treated means worked on and changed, so the letters of boil and acid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painful boil is being cauterised with acid, a hellish remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolic means devilish, belonging to the hellish underworld, so it matches infernal.

clue.text: Romantic sad about setter

indicators.note: about means around, so the gloomy word goes around the setter

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for dreary or sad
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: An idealistic person is gloomy about the puzzle compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealistic person with impractical fancies is called a romantic.

clue.text: Aliens endlessly turned around these days

indicators.note: around means wrapping about, so the shortened word goes round the next piece
endlessly drops the final letter of the word for turned

parts.note: turned upside down means inverse
AD, anno Domini, labels the current era

explanation.surface: Extraterrestrials keep spinning round and round in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' here is an adjective meaning upside down, not a sign to reverse; 'endlessly' trims it and 'around' wraps the shortened word about the era abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders from space are the aliens of science fiction, as in the arcade game.

clue.text: Endeavour to head left a bit

indicators.note: to head means to go in front of, so the detective's surname comes before the letter for left

parts.note: Inspector Morse's rarely used first name is Endeavour

explanation.surface: An instruction to try to steer a little to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour is the first name of Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of British television.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or mouthful, a little bit of something.

clue.text: Lands that produce extremely bankable pounds

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of bankable

parts.note: a head that pounds aches or throbs

explanation.surface: Property that earns a reliable sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' suggests money but is the verb meaning throbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat lands when it is run ashore on the sand, which is the verb sense here.

clue.text: Muscles of arms

explanation.surface: Talk of the muscles found in a person's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls big biceps by the word for firearms, and weapons generally are known by it too.

clue.text: He stops poaching meat and fish that's big enough

parts.note: game is the meat of wild animals and birds
an angler's keeper is a fish of legal size worth keeping

explanation.surface: A cook stops poaching once the meat and fish are large enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poaching' looks like a cooking method beside meat and fish, but it means illegal hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate's gamekeeper guards its birds and animals against illegal hunters.

clue.text: Condition of coasts ignored by uncompassionate criminal

indicators.note: coasts is ignored, its letters removed from the longer word
criminal means bad, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartless crook's state of being disregarded by those drifting past.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C, O, A, S, T, S out of UNCOMPASSIONATE and rearrange the remaining UNMPIONAE.
explanation.definitionFit: This lung infection is a medical condition.

clue.text: Lies hurt with nuts damaged

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of hurt and nuts are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone lying in pain with injured testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Untruths are falsehoods, the plural noun sense of lies.

clue.text: New quiet movement

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
peace means quiet, as in peace and quiet

explanation.surface: A fresh, silent campaign or political movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenpeace is an environmental campaigning organisation, a political movement.

clue.text: Coffee estate

definitions.meaning: the dregs left after brewing coffee
the land around a large house

explanation.definitionFit: Spent coffee leaves dregs called by this word, and an estate's land is called this too.

clue.text: Heard spies are often high

indicators.note: heard signals a word said aloud that sounds like another

parts.note: spies means sees, catches sight of

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that secret agents are frequently intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' suggests drugs but refers to rough water, as in the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Waves on open water are often called high, and the phrase high seas describes open ocean.

clue.text: Ways in which setters are devious

indicators.note: devious means not straight, so the letters of setters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble about how crossword compilers are crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: A way is a road, and roads in a town are its public thoroughfares.

clue.text: Content to assume tricolour is not imperial

indicators.note: the content of assume tricolour, the letters inside it, gives the answer

explanation.surface: Being happy to adopt a revolutionary flag is anti-imperial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imperial' suggests empire but means the old British system of measures.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal system of metres and grams replaced the imperial system of feet and pounds.

clue.text: Held by cox for directing crew

indicators.note: letters held by the words cox for directing are contained within them

explanation.surface: A rowing team is kept in line by the cox who steers it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's rowing crew races Cambridge each year in the Boat Race on the Thames.

clue.text: Scrap of fruit at half time

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
HT is the sports abbreviation for half time

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit eaten during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a small piece but means a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: Jesus is about to judge queen

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to deem is to judge or consider
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Christ is on the point of judging a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians call Christ the Saviour who buys back humanity from sin.

clue.text: Relief after last supper's overrun

indicators.note: after puts the relief word behind the final letter
last takes the final letter of supper

parts.note: aid is relief or help

explanation.surface: Help arrived after the Last Supper went on too long.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is an attack in which territory is overrun, a sudden incursion.

clue.text: Patching incorrect final draft in US

indicators.note: incorrect letters are wrongly arranged, so Patching is rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer is fixing errors in the last version of an American manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draft' is the American spelling of draught, a drink, not a written version.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is the last drink before bed, and draft is how Americans spell draught.

clue.text: Country-side supporter embraces church

indicators.note: something that embraces another holds it inside, so the side letter goes within the supporter

parts.note: a fan supports a team
R stands for right, one side
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rural team's follower is wrapped up in religion.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a European nation, the country where the British fought before Dunkirk.

clue.text: Steadies wobbling reserve

indicators.note: wobbling means unsteady, so the letters of Steadies are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone stabilises a wobbly support.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later use is to put it aside, the meaning of reserve as a verb.

clue.text: Billy's mains

definitions.meaning: belonging to Billy Ocean, the British pop singer
the main is a poetic word for the open sea, so mains are great seas

explanation.definitionFit: Billy Ocean is a pop singer, so his things are his; and the main is the high sea in old poetry.
